title: SaaS Backup Automation: A 2026 Guide
summary: SaaS backup automation secures critical cloud-hosted information by establishing independent, off-platform archives for your business data.
body_markdown:
## Building a custom backup workflow


Building a custom backup workflow requires connecting a scheduling trigger to a sequence of data extraction and storage actions within a no-code automation builder.


This process moves information from a proprietary cloud environment into a storage location where you control the file format and retention policy.


### Stage 1: Triggering the backup on a schedule


The workflow begins with the Schedule trigger. This initiates the process at a fixed cadence without human intervention. Trello offers internal "Butler" automations, but these are often restricted to actions within the board itself.


An external scheduler ensures the backup runs even if no one logs into the board. You define the frequency, such as every Sunday at midnight, so that the archive represents a consistent snapshot of project progress.


### Stage 2: Extracting data from the source application


Once triggered, the flow uses the Trello "Get Cards" action to pull all data from a specific board ID. This step retrieves the card names, descriptions, due dates, and custom fields that represent the actual intellectual property of the team.


To handle high volumes of data, the flow passes these cards into a Loop. This ensures the system processes every individual item rather than just the first few entries. This stage transforms the live, ephemeral board state into a structured data set ready for transport.


Activepieces handles this extraction across **748+ integrations** , allowing teams to move data to an environment they fully control.


Activepieces runs the same codebase on managed cloud or self-hosted via Docker and Kubernetes, ensuring that a backup pipeline built in the cloud can be moved to private infrastructure without rewriting the logic.


Where a flow runs should never decide whether you can leave the platform.

### Stage 3: Formatting and storing the archive file


After extraction, the flow uses the Google Docs "Create Document from Template" action to turn the raw JSON data into a readable format. Storing raw data in a proprietary database is a liability.


Placing it in Google Drive ensures the business can access the information using standard office tools. You must specify a Folder ID in Google Drive to keep these archives isolated from daily working files. This prevents the backup from being accidentally deleted during routine cleanup.


### Stage 4: Verifying the backup and sending alerts


The final stage uses a Router to check if the file creation was successful. If the Google Drive "Upload File" action fails due to a full drive or expired credentials, the flow follows the "High risk" path.


This triggers a Slack "Send Message" action to the DevOps channel. Nobody notices a silent failure in the API until it leads to a gap in the backup history. For successful runs, the flow sends a confirmation email via Gmail to the administrator.


This provides a direct link to the new archive for immediate verification.
